title: Would two creases on a folded sheet ever meet?
description: A square sheet is folded and opened, and pencil lines are drawn along the creases. The video ends on whether two of the lines would meet if they were drawn out beyond the paper, and it gives no answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: two straight lines drawn on a page may or may not meet when they are extended. Ask each child to guess and give a reason, and do not confirm any guess. Watch for students who think lines that do not meet on the page can never meet.

video_script.why: Before any word is named, the child meets two real lines on a folded sheet and has to say what happens when they are drawn out beyond the paper.
video_script.substitution: The book's own opening: fold a square sheet, draw pencil lines along the creases, and ask whether two lines would meet if extended beyond the paper.
video_script.anchor: A square sheet with pencil lines drawn along its creases, and two of the lines picked out.
never_show: any answer about the two lines
maths_rules: A square sheet is folded in different ways and opened, leaving straight creases.
Lines are drawn along the creases with a pencil and a scale, and any two of them are picked out.
The open question: would the two lines meet if they were extended beyond the paper. No answer is given or hinted.
video_script.design: One idea: two straight lines may or may not meet when they run on. The photo is a dimmed backdrop in the first beat and fades at its end; the drawn sheet arrives next and the two lines stay to the end.
